Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:1.hebrew: בכור מוכרין אותו - בזמן הזה, כדמוקי לה לקמן, [והכהנים] מוכרין אותו לכהן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:1.english: A firstborn [animal] may be sold - In the present era, as [the Gemara] establishes it later on, and the priests sell it to [another] priest.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:2.hebrew: תם חי - ולוקח ימתין עד שיפול בו מום וישחטנו, אבל תמים שחוט לא, דאין לו תקנה אלא קבורה, דאסור בהנאה, דקדשים השחוטין בחוץ הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:2.english: Unblemished, alive - And the buyer will wait until a blemish befalls it and [then] slaughter it. However, an unblemished [firstborn that was] slaughtered [may] not [be sold], for it has no remedy other than burial, as deriving benefit from it is prohibited, since it is [a case of] consecrated [animals] slaughtered outside [the Temple].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:3.english: And they betroth with it - Priests.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:4.hebrew: את האשה - דממונן הוא, דבעליו של בכור היינו כהן, דמשנולד הבכור שלו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:10:4.english: The woman - Because it is their property, for the owner of a firstborn is the priest, since from when the firstborn is born it is his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:11:1.english: They did not teach - that a living firstborn is the owners' property when it is unblemished, except in the present time.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:11:2.english: Ownership of them - While [they are] alive.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:12:1.english: And he raised an objection to him - We read [the text thus].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:12:2.hebrew: שהן ממונו - אפי' בזמן שבית המקדש קיים, דהא קרא דשבועת הפקדון בזמן שבית המקדש הוא דמחייב ליה אשם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:12:2.english: That they are his property - Even when the Temple is standing, for the verse of the oath of deposit obligates him [to bring] a guilt-offering [only] when the Temple is [standing].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:1.hebrew: ומשני רבינא - הכא דקתני דממון בעלים הם, בבכור הנולד בחו"ל בזמן המקדש עסקינן, דלא קאי להקרבה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:1.english: And Ravina answered - Here, where it teaches that it is the property of the owner, we are dealing with a firstborn born outside the Land [of Israel] during the time of the Temple, which does not stand for sacrifice.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:2.hebrew: ואליבא דר"ש דאמר - במסכת תמורה (דף כא.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:2.english: And in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon, who says - In Tractate Temurah (21a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:3.hebrew: אם באו - בכורות מחו"ל לא"י, תמימים יקרבו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:3.english: If they came - Firstborn [animals] from outside the Land [of Israel] to the Land of Israel, [if] unblemished, may be sacrificed.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:4.hebrew: באו אין לכתחילה לא - אלא ירעו עד שיסתאבו, והלכך, כיון דלאו להקרבה קאי, הוי ממון כהן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:13:4.english: [If] they came, yes; ab initio, no - Rather, they graze until they become blemished; and therefore, since it does not stand to be sacrificed, it is the property of the priest.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:14:1.hebrew: ואם איתא - דמחיים אמר רבי יוסי הגלילי דממון בעלים הן, כדקתני מתני' דחייבין על נזקן, ואוקימנא כר' יוסי הגלילי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:14:1.english: And if it is so - that [it was] while [they are] alive [that] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said that they are the property of the owners, as the Mishnah teaches that one is liable for their damage, and we established [it] in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:1:1.hebrew: הא קיימא לן - בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כו.) דמטלטלין נקנין עם הקרקע, ולא בעינן שיהו עומדין לתוכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:1:1.english: Don't we maintain - [In] the first chapter of Kiddushin (26a), that movable property is acquired along with land, and we do not require that it be situated within it:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:2:1.hebrew: אלא מאי אית לך למימר כו' - והשתא דבעל כרחך אתית להכי, אפי' תימא לאידך לישנא דעבדא כמקרקעי דמי, ודקשיא לך דשמואל, שאני מקרקעי דניידי ממקרקעי דלא ניידי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:2:1.english: Rather, what have you to say, etc. - And now that perforce you have arrived at this [distinction], you can even say according to the other version that a slave is like real estate; and as for that [statement] of Shmuel which was difficult for you, real estate that moves is different from real estate that does not move.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:5:1.hebrew: מעילה הוא - דבעינן דלא להוי בהו בנכסים שאני חייב בנזקין, הא אי לית בהו מעילה, אע"ג דמקדש קדשי, [אני] חייב בנזקין. כגון קדשים קלים שאין בהן מעילה מחיים אלא באימורין לאחר זריקת דם, כדגרסינן במסכת מעילה (דף ז:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:5:1.english: It is misuse - [Meaning] that we require that [misuse] not apply to them, [namely] to the properties [for which] I am liable for damages; thus, if [the prohibition of] misuse does not apply to them, even though they are consecrated, [I] am liable for damages — such as offerings of lesser sanctity, to which [the prohibition of] misuse does not apply while alive, but only to the sacrificial portions after the sprinkling of the blood, as we learn in Tractate Meilah (7b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:6:1.english: Who is the tanna - Who holds [one] liable for damages if his ox injured his fellow's peace-offering ox.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:6:2.english: They are the property of [their] owners - And we apply to it [the verse] "the ox of his neighbor."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:1.hebrew: ומעלה מעל בה' - וכחש בעמיתו וגו', גבי שבועת הפקדון כתיב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:1.english: And commits a trespass against the Lord - "and deals falsely with his neighbor, etc." — [it] is written regarding the oath of deposit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:2.hebrew: לרבות קדשים קלים - הא דכתיב בה', לרבות קדשים קלים, שאם הפקיד בהמת שלמים אצל חבירו, וכפר ונשבע והודה, משלם קרן וחומש ואשם. ואע"ג דבקדשי שמים אין נשבעין עליהן, כדגרסינן בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף נו.), בקדשים קלים נשבעין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:2.english: To include offerings of lesser sanctity - That which is written "against the Lord" [comes] to include offerings of lesser sanctity, [teaching] that if one deposited a peace-offering animal with his fellow, and [the fellow] denied [it] and swore [falsely] and [later] confessed, he pays the principal and an [added] fifth and [brings] a guilt-offering. And even though regarding consecrated [property] of Heaven one does not take an oath over them, as we learn in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 56a), regarding offerings of lesser sanctity one does take an oath.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:3.hebrew: שהן ממונו - של חבירו, וקרינן בהו: בה' וכחש, בעמיתו וכחש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:7:3.english: Which are his property - [The property] of his fellow, and we read regarding them [both] "against the Lord, and deals falsely" [and] "with his neighbor" [when] he deals falsely.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:8:1.english: One who betroths - a woman with his portion.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:9:1.hebrew: כי אמר ר' יוסי הגלילי - ממון בעלים הוי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:9:1.english: When Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said - [that] it is the property of the owners.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:9:2.english: When [it is] alive - For responsibility [for it] is upon him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:9:3.hebrew: אבל לאחר שחיטה - כי זכו — בין כהנים בחזה ושוק, בין בעלים בשאר הבשר — משלחן גבוה זכו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:9:3.english: But after slaughter - When they acquire [their portions] — whether the priests [acquiring] the breast and thigh, or the owners [acquiring] the rest of the meat — they acquire [them] from the table of the Most High.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:10:1.hebrew: ומחיים מי אמר - תימה: מאי קס"ד? אי מחיים לא אמר, כ"ש לאחר שחיטה! ואין לומר דה"פ: "ומחיים מי אמר, אפילו היכא דחזיא להקרבה? מדקמפלגת בין מחיים לאחר שחיטה, מכלל דמחיים אפילו בחזי להקרבה חשבת ליה ממונו, דומיא דלאחר שחיטה"; דאם כן, כי פריך מבכור, לסייעיה משלמים! דקאמר בן עזאי: "לא בא הכתוב אלא לרבות שלמים", ובן עזאי ואבא יוסי אתו לפרושי מילתיה דר"י הגלילי כדפ"ה, ושלמים חזו להקרבה, ואפילו לכתחילה יקרבו. וי"ל דה"פ: "ומחיים מי אמר במתנות כהונה, בחלק שיש לכהנים בשלמים?" מדלא קאמר "מתנות כהונה שאני", דהמקדש בחלקו היינו מתנות כהונה, חלק שיש לכהנים בשלמים, אלא קאמר משום דלאחר שחיטה משלחן גבוה זכו — משמע אבל מחיים הוי ממון בעלים, אע"ג דהוי מתנות כהונה. וא"ת: אי הוה משני "מתנות כהונה שאני", הוה משמע דחלק בעלים אפי' לאחר שחיטה הוי ממון בעלים; ובפ"ב דיו"ט (ביצה כא.) נמי אמר דבעלים משלחן גבוה זכו! וי"ל דה"מ לענין נדרים ונדבות, דאינן קריבים בי"ט משום דעיקר שחיטה הוי בשביל גבוה ולא משום אכילת בעלים, והוי "לכם" ולא לגבוה; אבל פשיטא דחלק בעלים אפי' לאחר שחיטה הוי ממון בעלים לקדש בו אשה ולכל דבר. וכן משמע דהמקדש בחלקו בחלק כהנים איירי, דלשון "המקדש בחלקו" לא שייך אלא בחלק כהנים, דבבעלים לא שייך בהן לשון "חלק", דעיקר הקרבן שלהן. וקראי נמי דמייתי בפ' האיש מקדש (קדושין דף נב:) אמתני' דהמקדש בחלקו: "וזה יהיה לך מקדש הקדשים מן האש" — לא כתיב אלא בכהנים. והא דקאמר התם: "לימא מתני' דלא כר' יוסי", ומסיק: "כי קאמר ר' יוסי מחיים, דיקא נמי דקתני המקדש בחלקו, דמשמע לאחר שחיטה" — לא הוי לפי המסקנא דהכא, אלא לפי מה דסלקא דעתיה מעיקרא; דלפי המסקנא, במתנות כהונה אפי' מחיים הוי ממון גבוה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:10:1.english: And while alive, did he say [so]? - [This is] astonishing: what was [the questioner] thinking? If he did not say [that it is the owner's property] while alive, all the more so [not] after slaughter! And one cannot say that this is its explanation: "Did he say [so] while alive, even where it is fit to be offered? Since you distinguish between while alive and after slaughter, it follows by implication that while alive, even when it is fit to be offered, you consider it his property, similar to after slaughter"; for if so, when he objects from a firstborn, let him support [Rabbi Yosei HaGalili] from peace-offerings! For Ben Azzai says: "The verse came only to include peace-offerings," and Ben Azzai and Abba Yose came to explain the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGalili, as Rashi explained, and peace-offerings are fit to be offered, and even ab initio they are offered. And one can answer that this is its explanation: "And while alive, did he say [so] regarding priestly gifts, [i.e.,] regarding the portion that the priests have in peace-offerings?" Since [the Gemara] did not say "priestly gifts are different" — for "one who betroths with his portion" refers to priestly gifts, [namely] the portion that the priests have in peace-offerings — rather, it said [that it is] because after slaughter they acquire [their portion] from the table of the Most High, it implies that while alive it is the owners' property, even though it is priestly gifts. And if you ask: If it had answered "priestly gifts are different," it would have implied that the owners' portion even after slaughter is the owners' property; yet in the second chapter of Yom Tov (Beitzah 21a) it also says that the owners acquire from the table of the Most High! And one can answer that that applies [only] with respect to vows and freewill-offerings, which are not offered on Yom Tov because the primary [purpose of the] slaughter is for the Most High and not for the owners' eating, and [the verse states] "for you" and not for the Most High; however, it is obvious that the owners' portion even after slaughter is the owners' property to betroth a woman with it and for everything. And so it is implied that "one who betroths with his portion" is speaking of the priests' portion, for the expression "one who betroths with his portion" is applicable only to the priests' portion, whereas with regard to the owners the expression "portion" is not applicable to them, since the main part of the offering is theirs. And also the verses that [the Gemara] cites in the chapter HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 52b) on the Mishnah of "one who betroths with his portion": "This shall be yours of the most holy things, from the fire" — [this] is written only regarding priests. And that which [the Gemara] says there: "Shall we say the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei?", and concludes: "When Rabbi Yosei said [it], it was while alive; it is also precise [from the wording], as it teaches 'one who betroths with his portion,' which implies after slaughter" — [this] is not according to the conclusion here, but rather according to what it initially thought; for according to the conclusion, with regard to priestly gifts, even while alive it is the property of the Most High:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:10:2.hebrew: תם חי אבל לא שחוט - הא לא איצטריך לאשמועינן, דבבכור בזמן הזה מוקמינן לה, דאין שייך בו מכירה לאחר שחיטה, דמיתסר בהנאה; אבל קמ"ל דמוכרין אותו חי, אע"ג דמעשר אין נמכר, דנאמר בו "לא ימכר ולא יגאל", וכן איתא בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ה:):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:10:2.english: Unblemished — alive, but not slaughtered - It was not necessary to teach us this [that it cannot be sold slaughtered], for we establish [the Mishnah] as referring to a firstborn in the present era, where selling is not applicable to it after slaughter because it becomes prohibited for benefit. Rather, it teaches us that one may sell it alive, even though [animal] tithe may not be sold, as it is stated regarding it, "it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed"; and so it is found in the first chapter of Temurah (5b).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:12:1.hebrew: ואיתיביה רבא לר"נ - ובזמן שבית המקדש קיים מיירי, דומיא דשלמים, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ח.); א"נ כדפ"ה, דלענין לאתויי קרבן מעילה קדריש קרא, דלא שייך אלא בזמן שבית המקדש קיים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:12:1.english: And Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman - And [it] is referring [to a time] when the Temple is standing, similar to peace-offerings, as we say in the first chapter of Temurah (8a); alternatively, [it is] as Rashi explained, that [the verse] is expounded with regard to bringing an offering for trespass, which is only applicable when the Temple is standing.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:1.hebrew: בבכור בחו"ל - הא דלא תירץ בבכור בזמן הזה, משום דדומיא דשלמים קתני כדפי' לעיל. אבל ר"נ דלעיל המ"ל בבכור בחו"ל, אבל זה הוא דוחק, וניחא ליה להעמיד בבכור בזמן הזה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:1.english: With regard to a firstborn outside of Eretz Yisrael - The reason [Ravina] did not answer [that the baraita refers] to a firstborn in the present day is because [the baraita] teaches [it as] similar to peace-offerings, as explained above. However, Rav Nachman above could have said [that the Mishnah refers] to a firstborn outside of Eretz Yisrael, but that is a forced [interpretation], and it was preferable to him to establish [it] as referring to a firstborn in the present day.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:2.hebrew: ואליבא דר"ש דאמר אם באו תמימים יקרבו - ור"ע פליג עליה בפ' אלו קדשים בתמורה (דף כא:), ואמר: לא יקרבו, דדריש מהקישא: מקום שאי אתה מביא מעשר שני, אי אתה מביא בכור. וא"ת: ואמאי קאמר "ואליבא דר"ש"? כ"ש אליבא דר"ע, דאמר לא יקרבו, דהוי ממונו! וי"ל: דמוקי לה כר"ש, משים דדומיא דשלמים קתני, דקריבים. ועוד י"ל: דע"כ לא מתוקמא כר"ע, מדמצריך קרא לרבויי שהוא ממון בעלים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:2.english: And in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says: If they came unblemished, they may be sacrificed - And Rabbi Akiva disagrees with him in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Kodashim in Temurah (21b), and says: They may not be sacrificed, for he expounds from a hekkesh [scriptural analogy]: [From] a place [from] which you do not bring second tithe, you do not bring a firstborn. And if you ask: Why does [Ravina] say "and in accordance with Rabbi Shimon"? All the more so according to Rabbi Akiva, who says they may not be sacrificed, it is his [the priest's] property! One can answer: He establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon because [the Baraita] teaches [the firstborn] as similar to peace-offerings, which are sacrificed. And furthermore one can answer: Perforce it cannot be established in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, from the fact that [the Gemara] requires a verse to include [the firstborn] as being the owner's property.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:3.hebrew: לכתחילה לא - פי': אין צריך להביאם, כדמפרש בפ' אלו קדשים (שם): "אמר ר"ש: מה טעם? לפי שכל הקדשים אין להם פרנסה במקומן" — פי': אין להם התרה אלא במקדש — "חוץ מן הבכור ומעשר שיש להם פרנסה במקומן" — פי': שנאכלין במומן. ולהכי תלי לה בר"ש, דכולה ר"ש היא. וקצת היה נראה לגרוס ר' ישמעאל, דהתם פריך אמתני' שאמר "יקרבו", מבן אנטונינוס שהביא בכורות מבבל ולא קבלם, ומשני: הא כר' ישמעאל, הא כר"ע; ומוכח התם שהמשנה כר' ישמעאל, וברייתא דבן אנטונינוס כר"ע:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:13:3.english: Not ab initio - Explanation: There is no need to bring them, as [the Gemara] explains in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Kodashim (ibid.): "Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason? Because all [other] consecrated offerings have no parnasah [remedy] in their place" — explanation: they have no permissibility [to be eaten] except in the Temple — "except for the firstborn and the [animal] tithe, which have parnasah in their place" — explanation: for they may be eaten in their blemished state. And therefore [the Gemara] attributes it to Rabbi Shimon, because the entire [statement] is Rabbi Shimon's. However, it would seem somewhat [plausible] to read "Rabbi Yishmael," for there [the Gemara] challenges the Mishnah, which said "they may be sacrificed," from [the incident of] Ben Antoninus, who brought firstborn animals from Babylonia and they did not accept them from him, and [the Gemara] answers: This [Mishnah] is in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, [and] that [baraita] is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva; and it is proven there that the Mishnah is in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, and the baraita of Ben Antoninus is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:14:1.hebrew: ואם איתא לישני ליה - פי': "ואם איתא" דמחיים הוי ממונו לר' יוסי הגלילי אפי' במתנות כהונה דחזו להקרבה, "לישני ליה" הא דר"נ אמר רבה בר אבוה כרבנן, דממה נפשך לא הוי כר"י הגלילי. ולפי סברא זו לא יהיה אמת הא דמשמע לקמן בסוף הפרה (בבא קמא דף נג: ושם) דבכור לא הוי בכלל "רעהו" אפי' בזמן הזה, דפליגי אביי ורבא בשור ושור של פסולי המוקדשין שנגחו, ופי' רבינו יהודאי גאון בבכור שור דלא פריק ליה, וכפי' צ"ל כמו שאפרש שם בע"ה; ומסתמא בימיהם פליגי, דבזמן הזה לכ"ע הוי ממון הדיוט. ומשני: "אלא מתנות כהונה שאני" — וה"ג ר"ח, ורש"י ל"ג כן. והשתא מלתיה דר"נ לא מיתוקמא אלא כר' יוסי הגלילי, ופלוגתא דאביי ורבא לקמן כרבנן. נראה דדוקא מחיים הוי לרבנן ממון גבוה, אפי' בעל מום דאסור בגיזה ועבודה, אבל לאחר שחיטה למה יחשב ממון גבוה אפילו בזמן שבית המקדש קיים? דהא אפילו לנכרי שרי להאכיל, כדתני' בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לג.) דאתקש לצבי ואיל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:14:1.english: "And if it is so... let him answer" - Explanation: "And if it is so" that while [it is] alive it is [considered] his property according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili even in [the case of] priestly gifts that are fit for sacrifice, "let him answer" that [statement] of Rav Naḥman [in the name of] Rabbah bar Avuha in accordance with the Rabbis, for either way it is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. And according to this reasoning, that which is implied later at the end of [the chapter] HaParah (Bava Kamma 53b and elsewhere) would not be true — namely, that a firstborn is not included in [the category of] "his fellow's" even in the present era, where Abaye and Rava disagree regarding an ox [of a private person] and an ox of disqualified consecrated animals that gored, and Rabbeinu Yehudai Gaon explained [it] as referring to a firstborn ox, which is not redeemed, and one must say [the law] according to his explanation, as I will explain there with God's help; and presumably they disagree regarding their own days, for in the present era according to everyone it is ordinary [private] property. And [the Gemara] answers: "Rather, priestly gifts are different" — and thus reads Rabbeinu Ḥananel, whereas Rashi does not read [it] thus. And now Rav Naḥman's statement is established only in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and the dispute of Abaye and Rava later is in accordance with the Rabbis. It appears that specifically while alive is it [considered] property of the Most High according to the Rabbis, even [when it is] blemished, since it is forbidden for shearing and labor; but after slaughter, why should it be considered property of the Most High even when the Temple is standing? For it is even permitted to feed [it] to a gentile, as it is taught [in a baraita] in the chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 33a), as it is compared to a deer and a ram.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:2:1.hebrew: שאני מטלטלי - פי' שיש להם דעת, אבל בהמות לא חשיבי מטלטלי דניידי, ונקנין באגב אפי' אין צבורים, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כו:): "טפח על טפח לפלוני ועמו מאה צאן":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:2:1.english: Movable property [that moves around] is different - [This] means [slaves,] who have intelligence; however, animals are not considered movable property that moves around, and they are acquired incidentally [along with land] even if they are not piled [upon it], as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (26b): "A handbreadth by a handbreadth [of land] to so-and-so, and with it one hundred sheep."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:3:1.hebrew: שאני מקרקעי דניידי - וא"ת: אפילו לא ניידי, הא תרי תשמישי נינהו. והוי כחולסית ומצולה, דמחזיק באחד מהן לא קנה האחר, כדאמרינן בפ' המוכר [את] הבית (ב"ב סז.) לחד לישנא? וי"ל: דעבד וקרקע חשיב חד תשמיש, לפי שהעבד ראוי לעבודת קרקע:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:3:1.english: "Land that moves around is different" - And if you ask: Even if they did not move around, they are two [different] uses, and it is like a sand field and a pond, where one who takes possession of one of them does not acquire the other, as we say in the chapter [entitled] HaMokher Et HaBayit (Bava Batra 67a) according to one version? And one can answer: A slave and land are considered one use, because the slave is fit for working the land.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:6:1.hebrew: מאן תנא - כלומר, פשיטא ליה דלא בא למעט ההקדשות דלית בהו מעילה, כגון קרקע; דכיון דהם נכסי גבוה, מעילה לא מעלה ולא מורדת:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 12b:6:1.english: Who is the tanna - That is to say, it is obvious to [the Gemara] that [the Tanna] did not come to exclude consecrated items that are not subject to me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property], such as land; for since they are property of the Most High, me'ilah neither adds nor detracts.
